focus: I will examine whether analog's marketplace advantage persists across horizons and headline membership, and whether recent price changes or provider counts identify where replacing the blend could reduce pinball loss while preserving the existing gate.

hypothesis.claim: For non-headline marketplace asks outside the 14-day gate, blending only analog and chronos will reduce pinball loss by combining forecasts of recurring repricing episodes with forecasts of persistence after those episodes subside.
hypothesis.expects: I expect improvement in both selection halves, enough changed cells to meet the breadth requirement, unchanged headline skill, and bootstrap support above 90%. Analog exceeds current skill at all three horizons in the targeted slice; chronos exceeds analog in both reported marketplace slices with four to twenty-one days since a change. These comparisons motivate the blend, but its joint loss and bootstrap support remain untested.
hypothesis.falsification: Reject if pooled skill fails to rise overall or in either selection half, fewer than 200 cells across at least five series change, headline pooled skill falls, or fewer than 90% of the 2000 ISO-week block bootstrap resamples show improvement.
hypothesis.mechanism: Provider repricing and offer turnover can move the offers determining the published median, producing sequences of changes followed by stable periods. The hypothesis is that analog captures recurring change sequences while chronos supplies useful forecasts after several unchanged days, making their blend more effective across these regimes than the current blend.
